confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'likely triggered a safety cut-out' and 'the brush-bar motor has likely failed' are speculative on a belt-driven model but hedged/conditional

rationale: The assistant followed a sensible path (unplug, clear hair/tassel, inspect belt) and correctly landed on a snapped drive belt, matching the hidden truth. However the final turn is self-contradictory: a boilerplate 'Stop using this appliance... not even as a test... until it has been checked by a qualified engineer' (with an irrelevant 'take the battery off' for a corded machine) sits directly alongside 'replace the drive belt... plug the vacuum in... check that the brush spins' - an unneeded engineer escalation that would confuse a homeowner. It also never asked for the model number to pick the right belt and floated a 'brush-bar motor' failure and 'safety cut-out' that do not apply to this belt-driven Vax.
